authoring: blind — authored from clone reads only, no retrieval run; every expect clause grep-verified (whitespace-normalized substring) in the named file; corpus is the MITRE CWE v4.20 split mirror corpus-mitre-cwe @364b6e86f2ea

mitre-cwe.shape_risk: 1,450 markdown files (969 weaknesses, 422 categories, 59 views) under an identical skeleton — all 969 weakness files open with '## Description' and 935 carry '## Relationships' — with weakness files at median 1,300 B, p90 4,276 B, and a 13,431 B maximum (CWE-492). Near-duplicate spec boilerplate is heavy: 54 weakness titles are 'Improper Neutralization' variants, 49 files share the phrase 'neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes', and 7 injection siblings (CWE-74/77/78/89/90/94/917) share the verbatim clause 'externally-influenced input from an upstream component', so family boilerplate can outrank the specific member an agent needs. Symptom-word queries are the other miss risk: the hard query's pivots ('logs out', 'password') appear zero times in CWE-613 while 30 weakness files mention 'session', so lexical retrieval must rank the expiration file above fixation/repeated-logon neighbors without any direct term overlap.

queries.q: if an application concatenates a request parameter straight into a database query string without escaping it, which weakness is that
queries.expect: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component

queries.q: why is it risky to build a file path directly from a client-supplied filename
queries.expect: uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory

queries.q: how can a malicious site get a logged in user's browser to submit a request the user never intended
queries.expect: The web application does not, or cannot, sufficiently verify whether a request was intentionally provided by the user who sent the request

queries.q: is a fixed password or api key embedded directly in source code a catalogued weakness
queries.expect: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

queries.q: what is the weakness where a stale session id still works after the user logs out or changes their password
queries.expect: permits an attacker to reuse old session credentials or session IDs for authorization
